title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-32
notes:
West leads the ♣Q against 4♥. East wins trick 1 with the ♣A and switches to the ♠10. West covers with the ♠J and dummy wins the ♠K. South's 2 spade losers are not going away so South must avoid the loss of a trump trick.

While there are combinations that allow South to draw trump without losing a trick, South's chances are much better if he can engineer a 3 card ending where the defense is on lead and must give up their natural trump trick.

Since East did not respond to his partner's opening bid and has already shown up with the ♣A, East's only possible other high card is the ♥J. West must have the ♦Q and South should finesse in that suit immediately, first cashing the ♦K. After cashing dummy's ♦A for a spade pitch, dummy's last diamond is ruffed.

South cashes the ♣K, pitching a spade from dummy, and ruffs his last club in dummy. South exits a spade, endplaying West. West can do no better than to cash his other spade trick and lead the ♥Q, a card he is known to hold.

South should rise with the ♥K and finesse East for the ♥J. If West held that card he would have a balanced 15 point hand and probably would have opened the bidding with 1NT.
